paper_metadata.title: A 0.45V 100-Channel Neural-Recording IC with Sub-μW/Channel Consumption in 0.18μm CMOS Dong Han1,2, Yuanjin Zheng1, Ramamoorthy Rajkumar3, Gavin Dawe3, Minkyu Je2,3

figures.label: Fig. 16
figures.caption: Figure 16.3.1 presents the design concept and block diagram of a 100-channel neural recording IC. For the neural-recording interface, the low-noise instrumentation amplifier (LNIA) requires a large current to achieve the desired inputreferred noise performance. However, the supply voltage can be low, as the signal swing is small. In contrast, the VGA needs a large supply voltage to accommodate the amplified signal, but the current supply can be low since the noise requirement is not critical. Therefore, to optimize overall power consumption, the LNIA and ADC operate with a low supply voltage (VDD=0.45V), and an internally boosted supply voltage 2VDD is used to operate the VGA. The maximum signal swings at V1 and V2 are 2VDD and VDD respectively. To accommodate this difference, a S/H network (Sw1-3), Cs and a comparator A1 are used to perform 1b DR folding. The operation procedure is as follows: (1) In the sampling phase, the bottom plate of Cs is connected to VDD by Sw3, and V1 is sampled to Cs through Sw1. The voltage across Cs becomes V1-VDD. (2) In the holding phase, A1 compares V2 with VDD. If V2>VDD, Sw3 is set to GND, resulting in V2=V1-VDD. Otherwise, Sw3 remains at VDD and V2=V1. Here A1 performs the pre-determination of the MSB before the ADC, and the A1 output becomes the MSB of the overall quantization. 2VDD is internally generated by a power-management circuit consisting of a 3-stack complementary DC-DC charge pump (CP) and an LDO. CP boosts VDD from the external to 3VDD, and then LDO regulates 3VDD to 2VDD. The offset voltage of the OTA in the LDO causes a small error (a few mV) in the 2VDD value. However, it only affects the VGA output common-mode (CM) and maximum swing, with no effect on the ADC accuracy. Due to the specified input and output voltage levels, the overall power efficiency of CP and LDO is 48%. Since the LDO load current is only 7% of the total channel current, the power efficiency of the power-management circuit has a minor effect on the overall power consumption. However, the power saved from this 2-level supply scheme (VDD for LNIA and ADC, and 2VDD for VGA) is significant. The input LNIA uses capacitive negative feedback and AC coupling [1] to set the closed-loop gain G1=C1/C3=100 and eliminate the input DC offset with a high-pass cutoff of 0.25Hz. 10-channel LNIAs share one VGA and ADC chain in a time-multiplexed manner using an analog MUX. The VGA uses C5-10 to achieve a closed-loop gain of 4 or 6. The input and output CM voltages of the VGA are 0.5VDD and VDD, 2003. respectively. The DC feedback with the gain of 2 by M7-8 sets the required DC condition. To reduce the VGA loading, the S/H network is implemented in a 2branch pipeline. The following SAR ADC consists of A1, a CDAC and a SAR con2010. trol logic block. The A1 is shared with the S/H network through S5. The CDAC has 8b resolution, resulting in 9b overall resolution.

references.sentence: Figure 16.3.1 presents the design concept and block diagram of a 100-channel neural recording IC.
Figure 16.3.2 shows a schematic of the OTA used in the LNIAs.
As shown in Fig. 16.3.3, the OTA used in VGAs operates with two different supply voltages.
(The chip micrograph is shown in Fig. 16.3.7.) Figure 16.3.4 shows the measured noise performance and frequency response of the LNIA and VGA chain.
Figure 16.3.5 shows the measured DNL and INL of the SAR ADC, and the summary of measured IC performances.
Figure 16.3.6 presents the recorded neural signal, which is reconstructed from the ADC output code and scaled for inputreferring.
A performance comparison with state-of-the-art neural-recording ICs [2-5] is also shown in Fig. 16.3.6.
